transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Sofia Ruiz (Redwood CSM); Paul Reynolds (Silverline Head of Platform), Anika Gupta (CTO), Marco Silva (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
- Quarterly review covering usage, cost trends, latency/reliability, and roadmap alignment.
- Main asks: pilot for checkout model, security docs, pricing for dedicated/reserved capacity, and technical benchmark.
- Next steps: pricing & security pack, schedule SE deep dive, customer to share traffic sample.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll give folks a minute. um — this is the qbr for Silverline, thanks for making time.
[00:12] Paul (Silverline): yeah thanks, Maya. busy week but wanted to make sure we beat our q3 goals — or q1 sorry.
[00:18] Sofia (Redwood): hi all, quick agenda: usage & cost trends, reliability and ops, roadmap alignment, and then open items / next steps.
[00:27] Anika (Silverline): sounds good. we mainly care about checkout latency and cost — those are the metrics leadership watches.
[00:33] Ethan (Redwood): great, i'll run the performance bit — quick note, some of the numbers come from our console telemetry which aggregates token usage, p95 latency, error rates. might be slight sampling noise.

[02:05] Ethan (Redwood): ok looking at Feb -> Mar, total token usage up about 28% month over month, most coming from the checkout assistant model. costwise hosted api spend rose accordingly. your usage pattern shows a lot of small requests — short contexts but high QPS during peak checkout windows.
[02:35] Marco (Silverline): yes that matches our observability, spikes at 11am and around 20:00 local. tail latency is the problem for us more than average - we see p95 occasional jumps to 800-1,200 ms.
[02:50] Ethan (Redwood): understood. on hosted we can mitigate some tail with prefix caching and smarter batching, but those strategies have tradeoffs. dedicated pools reduce contention and give you predictable p95s.

[04:10] Paul (Silverline): ok so dedicated is more predictable but pricier? what's the delta again, ballpark?
[04:18] Maya (Redwood): typically dedicated reserved capacity shows 20-40% lower unit cost at scale vs bursty hosted, depends on instance type and your sustained qps. important to note: reserved commit gives predictable throughput and is billed monthly, we can show concrete scenarios.
[04:35] Anika (Silverline): leadership wants a 30% cost improvement target while keeping p95 under 300 ms for checkout. is that realistic?
[04:44] Ethan (Redwood): 300 ms p95 is aggressive but achievable with dedicated pools + optimized quantized model variant and shorter context packing. we'd want to validate with a benchmark — run your real traffic through a staging cluster.

[06:00] Sofia (Redwood): also worth calling out route policies — you can keep the sensitive traffic in private deployment or VPC while routing lower-sensitivity workloads through hosted to save cost.
[06:14] Marco (Silverline): on the security side we need SOC 2 Type II, SSO via SAML, and KMS integration. plus audit logs retained for 12 months.
[06:25] Maya (Redwood): yep we support SOC2, SAML SSO, KMS integration, and audit logs. i'll share the security pack and the network diagram after the call.

[07:10] Ethan (Redwood): a quick note on quantization — we can often use 4-bit quantized weights which reduces GPU memory and cost, sometimes at a small accuracy hit. we'll run a regression check on your evaluation prompts.
[07:28] Paul (Silverline): regression is a concern — checkout templates are sensitive. we need a quality baseline and a set of guardrails.
[07:35] Ethan (Redwood): agreed — part of the pilot will include a quality evaluation set and rollback criteria.

[09:00] Anika (Silverline): can you remind me what the failover story is if a dedicated pool is saturated? we can't have orders failing.
[09:10] Maya (Redwood): we have smart routing and automatic fallback: if dedicated capacity hits thresholds, traffic can be routed to a compatible hosted variant, or to a lighter quantized model, depending on policy. that keeps the app up while preserving SLAs.
[09:30] Marco (Silverline): and billing — if we route to hosted temporarily, will costs spike unpredictably?
[09:38] Maya (Redwood): billing is transparent in the console; you can set hard caps and alerts. for budgets, reserved capacity smooths monthly costs; fallbacks will be charged at the hosting rate for the overflow, but we can set rules to cap spend.

[11:02] Ethan (Redwood): jumping to reliability — error rate has been steady around 0.3% for the month, with a couple of incidents tied to network flaps in region eu-west-1. we recommended enabling multi-region fallback for mission-critical routes.
[11:22] Paul (Silverline): multi-region sounds good but adds data residency complexity. we are required to keep PII in EU only.
[11:30] Maya (Redwood): understood; multi-region can be limited to within EU regions, or we can keep a private deployment on-prem for the PII workloads. we should map which endpoints handle PII and apply routing policies accordingly.

[13:00] Sofia (Redwood): quick ops note: your token spend per order has crept up because of verbose system prompts in a few models; tightening prompt templates could yield 8-12% immediate token savings.
[13:18] Paul (Silverline): oh that's interesting — we have a couple of service templates that include long example dialogs. we can trim those.

[14:05] Anika (Silverline): about the pilot: what do you need from us to start a 30-day pilot of the checkout model?
[14:15] Ethan (Redwood): ideal: a traffic sample (7 days preferred), a list of endpoints to test, SLA targets, and credentials to push testing to staging. we'll run baseline tests, then provision a dedicated pool with a quantized variant for comparison.
[14:35] Marco (Silverline): we can provide logs — i'll anonymize PII. timeline-wise we can start week of Mar 16.

[16:00] Maya (Redwood): perfect. recap on the business asks: 1) pricing scenarios for dedicated/reserved capacity, 2) security pack (SOC2 + network diag + KMS notes), 3) SE deep dive & benchmark plan, 4) pilot kickoff. We'll follow up within 48 hours.

[16:20] Paul (Silverline): sounds good. one more thing — we were evaluating alternatives like Bedrock and Anthropic for certain models. any notes on migration friction?
[16:32] Ethan (Redwood): migration work depends on model parity and SDK changes; we try to minimize lock-in with standard APIs and model catalogs. if you have a target model in mind we can compare perf and cost for a quick delta analysis.

[18:00] Anika (Silverline): on SSO, our IdP uses SAML 2.0 and SCIM provisioning. is SCIM supported?
[18:09] Sofia (Redwood): we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for user sync. i'll include the SSO integration guide in the security pack.

[20:00] Marco (Silverline): for benchmarks — can you provide the hardware spec you'll use for dedicated? we'd like to match it in our perf runs.
[20:10] Ethan (Redwood): yes, we'll propose GPU families and instance sizes. typical configs for your workload are A100-80GB equivalence or L40-like profiles — we'll include expected tokens/sec and p95 projections.

[22:00] Paul (Silverline): curious about caching — you mentioned prefix and KV cache earlier. how does KV cache interplay with multi-tenant hosted?
[22:10] Ethan (Redwood): KV cache is per-session on dedicated; on hosted we do shared caching with encryption boundaries. KV cache really helps for long context reuse, but for short checkout prompts the savings are modest. still worth evaluating for upsell flows.

[24:00] Maya (Redwood): quick pause for any blockers — Marco, do you foresee any infra blockers for the pilot?
[24:08] Marco (Silverline): main blocker is getting sanitized logs and a staging endpoint that mirrors prod traffic. if we can get a shared runbook and ephemeral creds, we can start.

[26:30] Sofia (Redwood): i'll own the onboarding runbook and send the checklist. it will include items for SSO, VPC peering if needed, and performance test steps.

[28:00] Paul (Silverline): one more ask: can you show us cost projections with and without quantization?
[28:08] Maya (Redwood): yes, we'll send a pricing sheet with three scenarios: hosted baseline, dedicated reserved, and dedicated + quantized. we'll call out likely accuracy deltas.

[30:00] Ethan (Redwood): on rollouts — we recommend canary deploy with traffic split and automated quality checks; if QPS or error rate exceeds thresholds, auto rollback kicks in. we'll help set the thresholds for your SLAs.

[32:00] Anika (Silverline): how real-time are the console metrics? our ops needs near-real-time traces for troubleshooting.
[32:08] Sofia (Redwood): console metrics are near real-time with a short ingestion lag (~30-60s). for full tracing we can ship traces to your datadog / prometheus.

[34:00] Marco (Silverline): ok let's talk about the data residency again — if we do dedicated in eu-west-1, will backups and logs remain in-region?
[34:10] Maya (Redwood): yes — we can scope storage and backups to the region, and for stricter requirements recommend private deployment. we'll document options in the security pack.

[36:00] Paul (Silverline): anything else on roadmap? we have a roadmap sync next week and want to ensure alignment.
[36:08] Maya (Redwood): our upcoming roadmap items relevant to you: console improvements (cost breakdown per-route), better autoscaling controls for dedicated, and quality-monitoring linked to evals. ETA Q2 for autoscaling tunables.

[38:00] Anika (Silverline): ok, last question — what does the contract look like for reserved capacity? min term?
[38:08] Maya (Redwood): typical terms are 3-12 month commitments, monthly billing with optional annual discounts. we can flex for enterprise negotiations. we'll include example T&Cs with the pricing email.

[40:00] Sofia (Redwood): recap and next steps: 1) Maya to send pricing scenarios and security pack (SOC2, SSO, KMS, network diag) — due 3/6. 2) Ethan to send benchmark plan and required data items — due 3/10. 3) Sofia to send onboarding runbook and checklist — due 3/8. 4) Silverline (Paul/Marco) to provide traffic sample + staging details — due 3/9.

[41:20] Paul (Silverline): thanks all. appreciate the clarity. we'll aim to have the logs to you by next Tue.
[41:28] Marco (Silverline): yeah i'll work with ops to scrub and share.

[42:00] Maya (Redwood): great, we'll follow up with a summary email and the attachments. anyone have final questions?
[42:10] Anika (Silverline): nope that's it for now.
[42:15] Sofia (Redwood): thanks everyone, we'll be in touch.
[42:20] End of call.
